decisions.reason: The existing message-843 MODIFY already removes the obsolete legacy connector-access constraints and records their non-applicability; no additional change is required.
The candidate already specifies one integrated board, and removing the separate legacy alignment requirement does not further change board topology.
The existing message-843 MODIFY directly records the resulting connector-placement freedom while preserving the explicit edge and grouping constraints.
Eliminating legacy interboard alignment does not alter the existing cost objective, integrated architecture, component policy, or connector-reduction strategy.
The antenna orientation and keepout remain explicit constraints regardless of general connector-placement freedom.
The source removes legacy interboard alignment, not the individual external sensor connectors or their integrated-board fanout role.
The task-local legacy BOM artifact and optional connector population are separate from the removed mechanical alignment requirement.

The stored measurement coverage still refers to separate main and sensor boards, but the source does not establish the integrated-board metering topology or resolve the existing uncertainty about omitting the INA monitor.
The obsolete interboard USB route was already removed when the integrated architecture was adopted; native USB programming behavior remains unchanged.
The backlight circuit and display behavior do not depend on legacy interboard connector alignment.
The earlier integrated-board transition already removed the interboard cable-length attribute and relocated the pull-ups; the source adds no further I2C change.
Battery protection behavior remains required and is independent of legacy board-to-board connector alignment.
